title: 3 things AI quietly eroded in my engineering team

scenes.narration: Leadership expected AI to make us several times faster. We tried agent swarms too. The speed-up never came, and I burned out.
Mid-year, I stopped asking what was wrong with my team, and looked at what AI had quietly taken from it.
First, the cost of building. It forced us to choose. Now every idea arrives as a working demo, and waits for a decision.
Second, the ladder of experience. Juniors sound sure. Seniors say: it depends. Guess who gets heard, and who fixes it later.
Third, asking each other for help. Those questions now go to a chat window. Faster, but that's how we got to know each other.
None of this shows up in a sprint report. It used to come for free. Now it has to be built on purpose.
I'm still positive about AI. But it's hard to adapt to something you haven't noticed.
